output.title: Why reviewer training is not enough
output.body:
Reviewer training helps, but it is only one control. If the same approval rule is applied over and over, the real weak point is often not knowledge. It is repeatable logic, data entry, fatigue, or edge cases. Training can improve judgment, but it does not change the workflow itself.

The useful question is simple: are most errors happening because the reviewer does not know the rule, or because the same rule still has to be checked manually every time? If it is the second case, you are looking at a workflow problem, not a classroom problem.

A plain example: if invoice or approval checks always follow the same sequence, a tired person can still miss one step. A repeatable rule check can catch that kind of miss; a slide deck cannot. That is not a criticism of people. It is just how late afternoons work.

At Bareni, we focus on repeatable logic steps in small-business workflows, with human approval kept in place for exceptions and high-risk decisions. That is a policy choice, not a guarantee.

So the next step is to identify one recurring decision step that follows the same logic each time and note how often it appears. If it is truly repeatable, it is worth separating from reviewer training before you spend more time on materials.
